en.html:
Night deepened.

After dinner, Kanae took out the instrument she had brought and began to play. Since our first meeting I had been wondering what the gigantic case she never let out of her reach could possibly hold. When the lid finally came open, the answer arrived with no ceremony at all. It was a double bass. Just that.

Why an occupation-force officer should walk around with a double bass, I could not say. Perhaps I should not even be asking. This was a woman who traveled with an attendant at her heels, so ordinary reasons were presumably not on offer.

She broke convention in everything, it seemed. The double bass was only the largest piece of evidence.

en.html:
An enemy of no small strength waited outside, and my body carried a wound of no small weight.

Even so, the hour was warm and gentle. For a moment I came close to remembering something that must not be remembered.

A scene far away, which I must not recall. A reality close at hand, which I must not forget: the fight still to come.

So, now, rest. Not to sink into comfort. For tomorrow's battle.

Now—sleep.

en.html:
Fuki went on with the washing beside me, looking a little dreamy about something. I went on splitting wood.

We had already made enough for the next several days. A larger stock would still do no harm.

Elder Yagenta was working inside the house. Mending one part or another seemed to be his morning routine. Ootori and her attendant were not here; they had gone back to the village during the night.

'We shall have to devise some method.'

Kanae's parting words crossed my mind on their own. With matters standing as they did, the magistrate's side would surely work on GHQ while buying itself time. That was the move to expect.

If they were allowed to, the village would not be saved. And my own objective would probably go unreached as well. Move at that leisurely pace and the time would arrive.

We needed a plan to pull out the enemy hiding in the sea of trees. I kept splitting wood and kept thinking.

en.html:
The hard voice that had been ringing in my head fell silent. I brought my attention back to my eyes, and found that the stack of firewood had grown to a considerable size.

Only three people lived here. This much would keep their fires lit for some time.

Funa stood holding the next log, looking up at me as if to ask a question. I nodded.

　意識を視界へ戻す――ふと見れば、積み上げられた
薪は随分な量に達していた。

　わずか三人の暮らし、これだけあれば当分炊きつけ
に困ることはないだろう。
　次の薪を抱えて問うように見上げてくる幼い視線へ、
頷きを返す。

弥源太"Mido. ...That is quite a lot of wood."
Kageaki"The young lady helped me. It was finished quickly."
ふな"I helped!"
弥源太"So you did. Shabaash. ...Mido, can I leave you in charge of the house for a while?"

弥源太"Yes. Down to the foothills. I should be back before noon."
Kageaki"Understood. I will keep the house."
弥源太"Sorry to ask. I leave it to you."

弥源太 「すまんな。 　よろしく頼む」

The old man went down the mountain path with steady steps. A small cloth bundle was tucked under one arm.

Something white stuck out of its edge. White. A flower.

Visiting a grave? Rather late for the higan-e, though...

危なげのない足取りで、山道を下りてゆく老人。
　脇に少々の手荷物を抱えていた。小さな風呂敷包み。

　その端から何か、白いものが突き出している。
　白い――花。

　墓参りだろうか？
　<ruby>彼岸会<rt>ひがんえ</rt></ruby>にはいささか遅過ぎるが……。
